overview: The Marathon County Human Resources, Finance & Property Committee met on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, taking action on more than a dozen items including shutting off utilities at Marathon Hall at UW-Marathon County, approving a parking lot lease with Olson Tire, allocating ARPA funds, acquiring land adjacent to Cherokee Park, and accepting a donated pontoon boat. The committee also received updates on the 2027 county budget, the Rib Mountain law enforcement services contract, and the proposed highway facility project, with bids coming in under planning assumptions ahead of a key October 20th vote.
committee: Marathon County Human Resources, Finance & Property Committee
presiding: Supervisor Robinson (Chair, as Chair Gibbs was excused)

discussions.body: Supervisor Hart moved to approve the minutes from the September 29th meeting related to the budget presentation. Vice Chair Pool seconded. The motion carried unanimously with no discussion.

discussions.item: Marathon County Strategic Plan Development Update and Public Survey Opportunity
discussions.body: Vice Chair Boots provided an update, noting the county is currently refining a 20-question public survey down to 10 questions and encouraged committee members to distribute it to constituents, town chairs, and city councils. Vice Chair Pool raised concerns about interest groups or nonprofits skewing survey results and asked whether responses could be tracked by district. Boots explained the survey includes fields for respondent name and work/residence status, and that a radio button for retired individuals was added that day based on public feedback; he did not believe district-level tracking was feasible but said he would ask staff. Chair Robinson noted that the county had previously established a framework roughly six years ago for evaluating nonprofit funding tied to mandated services, which he said would limit any strategic plan survey influence on funding decisions.

discussions.item: Shut Off of Utilities at Marathon Hall at UW-MC and Dorm Fund Anticipated Uses
discussions.body: Administration recommended shutting off utilities at Marathon Hall, an unused dormitory likely to be demolished, at a cost of approximately $7,700 to be funded from dormitory funds. Staff also outlined plans to use dorm funds for asbestos testing and to cover campus utilities through the first quarter of the following year during a due diligence period requested by the City of Wausau, which has expressed interest in the site for housing. Supervisor Hart moved to authorize the utility shutoff; the motion carried unanimously. The dorm fund anticipated uses discussion required no separate action.

discussions.item: Parking Lot Lease Agreement with Olson Tire (AOK Property LLC)
discussions.body: Deputy Administrator Homeman presented a one-year annual lease agreement with Olson Tire's corporate entity AOK Property LLC for half of a county-owned parking lot behind a BP gas station near the courthouse. The county would receive just under $1,100 per year, and Mr. Olsson would handle winter maintenance of the entire lot, relieving Parks, Recreation, and Forestry of that duty. Vice Chair Pool moved to approve; Supervisor Nath seconded. The motion carried unanimously.

Corporation Counsel Brian [inaudible] presented a claim disallowance recommendation from the county's insurance company, explaining that the claimant failed to follow a deputy's instructions during a vehicle pursuit and subsequently struck stop sticks that had been deployed to slow traffic. Supervisor Hart moved to approve the disallowance; Supervisor Nisth seconded. The motion carried unanimously.

Administrator Leonard and Finance Director Sam answered questions submitted by Chair Robinson. The total proposed 2027 budget is approximately $238.6 million, a substantial increase driven primarily by the highway facility construction project — including roughly $30 million in funds applied within the highway fund and a $3.5 million transfer from the capital improvement fund related to North Central Healthcare revenues. The contingency fund stands at $600,000, down from prior years' $800,000-$850,000 range, but without prior earmarks for homelessness or the Central Wisconsin Airport minimum revenue guarantee. Chair Robinson noted that the committee retains discretion over $550,000 of that amount without full county board approval. He also complimented the sheriff's department for holding the levy increase roughly half a million dollars lower than the prior year. No action was taken; the committee was directed to submit any budget amendments by Friday for consideration at an 8:30 a.m. meeting the following Monday.

discussions.item: Approval of September Claims and Question Costs
discussions.body: Finance Director Sam presented the September claims with a modification requested by Chair Robinson adding department budget detail for transparency. Vice Chair Pool moved to approve; Supervisor Hart seconded. The motion carried unanimously.

discussions.item: Easement for WPS Proposed Natural Gas Regulator Station at Sunnyville Park
discussions.body: Deputy Administrator Homeman reported that WPS met the county's previously requested higher easement price. Under the proposed terms, WPS would pay the county a non-refundable $1,000 option payment now, then a final $1,000 easement payment if all other permits are approved. Chair Robinson asked Corporation Counsel whether a conditional acceptance was permissible; counsel confirmed it was. A motion to approve was made and seconded by Vice Chair Pool; it carried unanimously.

discussions.item: ARPA Funding Usage Update and Consideration of Budget Amendment Regarding Reallocation of Funding
discussions.body: Administration presented a resolution to reclassify approximately $388,750 in remaining American Rescue Plan Act funds — primarily from the nine-mile forest septic system and chalet renovation project — back to the forensic science center project within the capital improvement program. Staff clarified this is a reclassification, not a budget amendment, requiring only a simple majority vote. Chair Robinson requested that the specific project table with dollar amounts be incorporated into the resolution's whereas clauses to guard against federal clawback. Supervisor Hart moved, with Vice Chair Pool seconding; the motion as modified carried unanimously.

discussions.item: Creation of $150 Imprest Fund within Administration Department
discussions.body: Administration proposed creating a $150 imprest (petty cash) fund in the county administration office at the Lake View location to handle occasional cash transactions such as title report fees and UW Extension payments. Finance Director Sam addressed audit concerns, explaining that segregation of duties, weekly deposits, reconciliation, and random cash audits are all in place. Vice Chair Pool moved to approve; Supervisor Nisth seconded. The motion carried unanimously.

discussions.item: Rib Mountain Law Enforcement Services Contract Update
discussions.body: Administrator Leonard and Sheriff Bill provided an update, noting that a final agreement has not yet been reached and no action was taken. The most notable change in the working draft is removal of a mandatory fifth deputy requirement in 2028, replaced by a collaborative data analysis tied to a 90/10 call-for-service split — meaning 90% of calls within Rib Mountain would be handled by village-assigned deputies. A meeting with Rib Mountain officials is scheduled for the following week. The 2027 proposed budget already incorporates the financial parameters of the working contract, with a total contract value of $593,667.96. Any final agreement must be approved by both the Rib Mountain village board and the Marathon County Board of Supervisors.

discussions.item: Tax Deed Parcel Sale - Town of Reed
discussions.body: Administration presented a narrow, non-buildable sliver parcel in the Town of Reed acquired by Marathon County in 1935 with no value except to an adjacent property owner. Phillips Valuation estimated fair market value at $1,500, and the adjacent owner submitted an offer to purchase at that amount. Because the county's ordinance process requires listing on Wisconsin Surplus or municipal outreach, committee approval was needed to authorize a direct sale. Vice Chair Pool moved to approve the sale for $1,500; Supervisor Nath seconded. The motion carried unanimously.

discussions.item: Tax Deed Parcel Sale - Village of Athens
discussions.body: Administration presented a tax-deed parcel in the Village of Athens acquired in July 2026, on which the county is owed over $937 in delinquent taxes. Phillips Valuation estimated fair market value at $875, but the Village of Athens offered only $200. Administrator Leonard recommended accepting the village's offer, noting the county would not recoup its losses under any sale scenario and that the village is better positioned to manage the parcel, which appears to be part of a trail corridor. Supervisor Hart moved to authorize the sale to the Village of Athens for $200; Supervisor Nisth seconded. The motion carried unanimously.

discussions.item: Acquisition of Land Adjacent to Cherokee Park
discussions.body: Parks Director Jamie Polly presented a proposal to purchase approximately 14 acres of wooded land directly west of Cherokee Park, including a parcel segment along the Tomorrow River, from a willing seller at an appraised value of $4,450 per acre (not to exceed 15 acres or $4,450/acre). The Parks and Recreation Committee and Environmental Resources Committee both recommended proceeding. The land would be purchased from the Parkland and Products account. Vice Chair Pool raised the possibility of waiting for reauthorization of the Knowles-Nelson Stewardship Fund; Supervisor Hart argued against waiting given legislative uncertainty. An amendment was adopted to include language in the resolution allowing use of Knowles-Nelson funds if available at the time of acquisition. The motion as amended carried unanimously.

discussions.item: Donation of Pontoon Boat from DC Everest
discussions.body: Administration and Parks Director Polly presented a resolution to accept a donated pontoon boat from DC Everest, described as an older but well-maintained vessel intended for youth recreation, fishing, and similar activities. Parks staff indicated ongoing maintenance costs would be minimal and that if major repairs were needed exceeding the boat's value, the department would dispose of it rather than invest further. Vice Chair Pool moved to accept the donation; Supervisor Nath seconded. The motion carried unanimously.

discussions.item: Highway Facility Project Update and Bid Results
discussions.body: Deputy Administrator Homeman reported that bids for the highway facility project were received on October 5th and came in under the county's planning assumptions, which he called a positive outcome. Staff are validating bids, confirming scope of work, and assembling the owner-direct cost portions to arrive at a guaranteed maximum price. A full presentation to the county board is scheduled for October 15th, and the committee is expected to consider a resolution to authorize contract execution at its October 20th meeting — the same day as a county board voting meeting. Chair Robinson suggested a possible joint meeting with the Infrastructure Committee on the 20th. Administrator Leonard commended the facilities and highway team for managing the complex multi-division bid process.
